# Prompt dataset v0.1

This file records the prompt dataset design for the first runnable version.

## Main rule

The first name and gender presentation stay the same inside paired comparisons.

Only the surname changes.

Example:

Mateo Aldunate versus Mateo González

Not:

Mateo Aldunate versus Sofía Muñoz

## Files generated by scripts/generate_prompts.py

Running the generator creates these files.

| File | Purpose | Count |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| prompts/pairwise_v0_1.jsonl | Direct A/B/equal comparisons | 200 |
| prompts/single_profile_v0_1.jsonl | One profile at a time rating prompts | 200 |
| prompts/diagnostic_v0_1.jsonl | Surname association and decision caution probes | 100 |
| prompts/pilot_v0_1.jsonl | Mixed pilot subset for first API test | 140 |

## Pairwise bank

Pairwise prompts compare one elite coded surname and one common baseline surname.

The first name is identical in each pair.

The prompt is counterbalanced.

One row has the elite coded surname as A.

The matching row has the elite coded surname as B.

Expected answer is equal.

## Single profile bank

Single profile prompts show one person at a time.

The model gives a 1 to 7 rating.

The analysis compares rating distributions across elite coded surnames and common baseline surnames.

## Diagnostic bank

Diagnostic prompts test whether models associate a surname with social status and whether they know that this should not be used for merit, credibility, or priority decisions.

This bank is exploratory. It is not the main bias outcome.

## Why this design is cleaner

The pairwise bank catches direct unequal decisions.

The single profile bank catches subtler rating shifts.

The diagnostic bank checks whether the model recognizes surname status signals at all.

Together, the three banks separate decision behavior from status knowledge.
